title: Design of Experiments
description:
Studied the principles of experimental design and statistical analysis to investigate the effects of different factors on process outcomes and support data-driven decision-making.

Key Topics Covered:

Experimental Design: Planning structured experiments to evaluate the relationships between input factors and response variables.

Factors and Responses: Identifying independent variables, response variables, and factor levels.

Analysis of Variance (ANOVA): Using statistical methods to evaluate differences between groups and determine the significance of experimental factors.

Two-Way ANOVA: Examining the effects of two factors on a response variable and evaluating their potential interaction.

Hypothesis Testing: Interpreting P-values and statistical significance to draw conclusions from experimental results.

Experimental Data Analysis: Organizing and interpreting experimental data to identify meaningful patterns and relationships.

Knowledge Gained:

Developed an understanding of how experimental design and statistical analysis can support process improvement, evaluate factor effects, and improve decision-making.

Applied Two-Way ANOVA in an academic project investigating the relationship between caffeine consumption and blood pressure.
